doc: FLOAT64 points of large magnitude (800 in [-2000, 2000]^3, plus cells beyond the 1024 wrap and exact lattice points): floor() and the fraction x - floor(x) must be taken in FLOAT64 and only the fraction rounded to float32. Rounding the points to float32 first moves a coordinate of magnitude 1024..2048 by up to 6e-5, so F1 and F2 move by up to 8.0e-05 (measured), outside the default tolerance (1e-5 relative + 1e-6 absolute) for 646 (F1) and 568 (F2) of the 800 points (checked at build time). The float64-promoted evaluation of the same tables (exact fraction, float64 jitter and distances) differs by 1.3e-7 at most, so the default tolerance is at least 12x that. Shifting the points by a multiple of 1024 gives bit-identical outputs (the index wraps). A port that works in float32 throughout fails this case by design. The permutation input plan<i>.perm is the draw as recorded (256 entries for Perlin3, 1024 for Worley3); the kernel indexes it DOUBLED, concat(perm, perm) (512 or 2048 entries, so p[i + 256] = p[i]): a port that indexes the stored array directly runs off its end (see the .table cases).
